G-F1.title: Out-of-sample skill — leave-one-province-out, 2025 cross-section
G-F1.detail: 38 province folds over 514 regencies. A random k-fold on the same rows reaches R² 0.6526 — the inflation a non-spatial fold buys, and the reason this number is the one published. Where the error lives: 57% of the squared error is a single constant offset for a whole province, and once that offset is removed the model orders regencies inside their province at ρ 0.50.

G-F2.title: Java / off-Java and urban / rural skill disclosed separately
G-F2.detail: A disclosure gate: it is satisfied by measuring and publishing both sides, and a red value below is a finding, not a gate failure. kota skill sits under 0.35, so every kota estimate is labelled indicative. Urban R² of -0.5993 is below zero — for kota the model does worse than predicting the national mean, and city estimates should be read as indicative only.

G-F3.title: Temporal hold-out — train ≤ 2023, predict 2024 and 2025
G-F3.detail: Fitted on 2016–2023 only, then asked for the two releases it has never seen. Read the first two rows with care: the same regencies appear in training in earlier years and the roof and land-cover layers are single-vintage, so what they mostly measure is how persistent a regency's rate is. The last two rows are the strict version — the province is held out as well as the year — and that is the number to quote to a client.

G-F4.title: Benchmark integrity — kecamatan estimates reproduce every official regency rate
G-F4.detail: Population-weighted mean of the kecamatan estimates recomputed from the shipped file for all 5,140 regency-years.
